author: TheWholeFnShow
what_it_is: All the skaters have full stats, 30 tapes, and 3 gold medals. Just load it up and have fun.
format: DexDrive .n64: "123-456-STD" and a 0x1040-byte header (DexPlorer comments), then a 32 KiB Controller Pak: note NTFE/52 "TH-ETR", 11 pages, with no extension (the game writes its career notes with extension G); ID block checksums 0101/FEFD

verified.converted_with: tools/gamefaqs/n64-dexdrive.py convert tony-hawks-pro-skater.903.n64 OUT: dexdrive: pak = the 32768 bytes after the 0x1040-byte header; ID block checksums 0101/FEFD wrong in every copy, rewritten as 0101/FEF1

converted_standalone.how: the same bytes as the .srm regions, as standalone Mupen64Plus keeps them: <GoodName (32 chars)>-<MD5 8>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk in its save folder

verified.baseline: with no save: LOAD GAME says NO TONY HAWK GAME NOTES FOUND.

mupen64plus-next.detail: Career Mode > LOAD GAME: "NO TONY HAWK GAME NOTES FOUND." The note TH-ETR is on the pak but has no extension, and the game lists only notes with extension G (its own saves and the TH-TP note on GameFAQs 725 have it). Diagnostic, not a conversion: with that one byte set to G the game lists "ETR" (checked in Mupen64Plus-Next). The pak as downloaded (ID checksums 0101/FEFD) first gets "A damaged Controller Pak or an unsupported device is connected ... Attempt to repair?"

note: The note has lost its extension byte (the game writes G), so Tony Hawk's Pro Skater lists no career notes: the file's fault, not the cores'. The pak's ID checksums are DexPlorer's (FEFD) and were rewritten (as downloaded the game first offers to repair the pak). The revision is not recorded; Rev 1 used.
